## The bounded Newton step (`constrained_newton_step`) {#sec-ch10-newton}

### Summary

A Newton iteration on mole amounts must not drive an amount negative. kintera first solves the square Newton system
directly, which keeps full precision. It keeps that direction unless the direction leaves a bound that is already
active, and only then falls back to the constrained least squares of @sec-ch10-kkt. A second function forms the
trial state along the step and rejects it if a bound or a step-size limit is broken, so that the caller can shorten
the step.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** A Newton direction that respects active bounds, @eq-ch10-newton-usable.

**Data.** Square $\mathsf J$ ($n \times n$), right-hand side, constraint rows $\mathsf C$ and bounds $d$.

**Placement.** The phase-equilibrium Newton loop (@sec-ch05).

**Activation.** Always; `reg` defaults to 0.

**Guarantee / limits.** Direct solve when usable; otherwise status of `leastsq_kkt`.

**Evidence.** `test_thermo`; see the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $\mathsf J$, the Newton matrix; $g$, its right-hand side; $p$, the direction; $c_i$, row $i$ of the
constraint matrix; $d_i$, its bound; $s$, the step scale; $z$, the state; $\theta$, the floor; $r$, `max_ratio`.

### Derivation

The direct direction is $p = \mathsf J^{-1} g$, from `dsolve_lu` of @sec-ch10-dense. It is kept when it is finite and,
for every constraint $i$ with $d_i \le 0$,

$$
c_i\, p \le 0 ,
$$ {#eq-ch10-newton-usable}

that is, unless it points out of a bound with no slack left. The reason is one line. Along the direction the
constraint value grows as $c_i(z + s\,p) = c_i z + s\,c_i p$, so a row with slack $d_i > 0$ and $c_i p > 0$ is still
met for every scale $s \le d_i/(c_i p)$, which the caller's step reduction can reach. A row with no slack,
$d_i \le 0$, and $c_i p > 0$ is crossed by every $s > 0$; only such rows send the step to the constrained solve. @eq-ch10-newton-usable is tested in
`constrained_newton_step` ({{< code src/math/constrained_newton.h constrained_newton_step >}}). Otherwise the step
solves $\min \lVert \mathsf J p - g \rVert$ with $\mathsf C p \le d$ by `leastsq_kkt` with no equality rows.

The trial state uses the same sign convention as the constraints:

$$
z_i^{\mathrm{trial}} = z_i - s \sum_j c_{ij}\, p_j .
$$ {#eq-ch10-newton-trial}

@eq-ch10-newton-trial is computed in `constrained_newton_trial`
({{< code src/math/constrained_newton.h constrained_newton_trial >}}).

### Numerical method

1. `constrained_newton_step` copies $\mathsf J$ and $g$, calls `dsolve_lu`, and checks finiteness and
   @eq-ch10-newton-usable. If the direction is usable, it is returned with `max_iter` set to 1.
2. Otherwise `leastsq_kkt` runs on the original arrays with $n_1 = n_2 = n$ and `neq` 0.
3. `constrained_newton_trial` rejects the trial if any entry is non-finite or negative. It also rejects it if one of
   the first `npositive` entries is not above the floor. When $r > 0$, it rejects a change by more than a factor $r$
   in either direction of the first `nlimited` positive entries.

The step scale and its reduction belong to the caller. The figure is not provided: the figure module is not written
yet.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_thermo` | `LeastSquaresKkt.DirectlySolvesIllConditionedSquareSystem`: direct path, one iteration | absolute $10^{-6}$ | the test |
| `test_thermo` | `LeastSquaresKkt.LineSearchCanScaleNewtonDirectionToBound`: unit trial rejected, half step accepted | exact | the test |

: Tests of the bounded Newton step. {#tbl-ch10-newton-tests}

The cases are in {{< code tests/test_thermo.cpp >}}. `check_ch10_dense.py` checks both branches: "(j)
constrained_newton_step: bounds with slack keep the direct solve (status 0, iters 1, diff 1.1e-16); zero-slack bounds
crossed -> KKT (status 0, diff to brute force 1.4e-17) (tol 1e-10) PASS".[^ch10-newton-check]

### Limits

- A direction may leave a bound with slack; only the caller's step reduction keeps the state feasible.
- The fallback ignores the direct solution and starts the active-set solve from scratch.
